summary: Mother Sayamagyi (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under and succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin, and taught Roger Bischoff.

Motohiro Yoritomi (1945–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (BA, MA, PhD) under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He held professorships at Shuchiin University and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Motoi Ono (born 1958) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima, completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tsukuba, and earned a Dr.phil. from the University of Vienna before joining Tsukuba's faculty around 1999.
Moumita Hossain works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and was a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society as attested in 2026.

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1975) and lectured in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982, 1994).

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, and held posts at the University of Leipzig, Heidelberg University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Muhamad Saputra is an academic who studied as a PhD student under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron at the Australian National University (attested 2026).

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director at Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Muhammad Nasim Khan is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an M.Phil from the University of Peshawar, later serving there as Assistant Professor of Archaeology, with posts at Hamburg and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Mukund Lalji Wadekar is an Indologist. He served as Officiating Director at both the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002–2008) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008), and was General Editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series.
Mukund Ram Shastri (died 1921) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Head Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, attested in 1911 and 1916–1918.

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1978), president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies.

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA), and the University of Queensland, where he earned an MA and PhD under Roderick S. Bucknell.

Munenobu Sakurai (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University, later serving as an associate professor at Iwate University (~1994–2004) and as a professor at Tohoku University (~2005).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was a scholar in Indology and computational fields. He studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University (PhD), and held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1980–1988) and Kyoto University (~1988–2009).

Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki around 1909 and attended the University of Tokyo from around 1910 to 1913.

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall, attested in 2010.

Munis D. Faruqui (born 1967) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2004) and as Director and Sarah Kailath Chair at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

Munish Chandra Joshi (1935–2007) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1989–1993) and Member Secretary at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1995–2000).

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) specialized in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, he taught Latin at Yale and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1940 to 1971.
